# Ship of Theseus — Amend or Supersede

<p class="lens-meta"><code class="lens-code">THESEUS</code> · Greek — Socratic and Aristotelian · <strong>Catalogued — a reading, owns no gate</strong></p>

## The failure it names

silent identity drift: a claim's meaning changes across edits while its id, and everything citing it, stays put

## What it does

editing an accepted claim's proposition forces an explicit amend-or-supersede decision

## Worked example

forensicnomicon's ChangeType already types this for artifacts, and its BehaviorChanged variant — semantics changed without format change — is exactly the drift that leaves every downstream citation pointing at something it no longer says.

## Sources

- Plutarch, Life of Theseus 23.1
- <https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/identity-over-time/>
